_what_this_is: The measured-constants keeper (stream F, seed). One JSON object per constant that a deployed copy of the harness restates. This file is the canonical value; every consumer is either derived from it or compared against it. It exists because a corrected fact did not reach the copies that act on it: the refuted 0.81 GB figure survived two independent refutations in five deployed copies of the skill the default path loads, with no correction marker (A Part 3.1, B section 0, D defect D10).
_rules: NEVER delete a superseded value. Record it in `supersedes` with its value, the figure that carried it, and the document that measured it wrong. A refuted constant that a reader can see refuted is a warning; a refuted constant that was deleted is a constant that comes back.

Where two live surfaces publish different answers to the same question, record BOTH in `unresolved` with both sources. This keeper makes the disagreement visible; it does not arbitrate it. Arbitration requires a measurement, and a measurement is not a JSON edit.

`confidence` is either an interval string (the value was measured) or the literal word "reasoned" (it was derived from measured inputs). A prediction must be labelled as one. A prediction presented as a measurement is the failure this whole exercise exists to stop.
`measured_at` is the date the measurement was taken, not the date the document that quotes it was written.
Provenance: `source` names a document and a section. A value with no source is refused, not stored.
Values are held in their measured unit. Converting units at this layer is how the 14-slot units error happened (84 section 4.3, D section 3.3.2).

how_to_use.intended_enforcement: A checker that reads this file, resolves each entry's `restate_glob`, and fails (non-zero exit) when a deployed copy restates the constant with a value that is neither (a) the canonical `value`/`value_interval`, nor (b) named inline as superseded. The comparison must be a property of the output text, not a shape test (V3): extract the stated number from the copy and compare it to the canonical number, rather than grepping for the presence of a string. It must also fail when an entry's `supersedes` values are present in a deployed copy WITH NO correction marker - the specific defect that kept 0.81 GB alive - and it must be runnable in every reader class that loads the copy: local Interactive, ssh-spawned, and scheduled task (a profile check is only evidence for the logon class that ran it; 106 section 8). The negative half matters more than the positive half: a keeper that never reds is the same class of object as the sixteen green checks over broken things catalogued in D section 3.7. Per V4, this keeper must be demonstrated failing against a deliberately hand-edited copy before it is trusted.
how_to_use.does_such_a_checker_exist_today: NO. Verified 2026-09-18 on ZABZ-YOGA, read-only. What exists and was checked: (1) `scripts/harness-verify.ps1` is a real invariant checker with 11 `Check` blocks and exits non-zero on failure - but it validates GENERATED/deployed ARTEFACTS (preset-in-sync, MCP rows, reaper task, sampler heartbeat, journal lock, bundle resolution, primary-port ownership, commit-vs-physical, stale MCP gens, preset-deployed-to-~/.dsh, bundle declarations) and contains NO check on any measured constant in any document, README or skill file. Its closest text, at line 206, prints 'measured: idle commit floor ~18 GB; ~0.58 GB commit per extra node process' as a STRING inside a check whose actual assertion is commit < physical - it documents the correction in prose and asserts nothing about it. (2) No scheduled task runs it: `Get-ScheduledTask` filtered to pwsh/powershell actions returned exactly one task, `DSH Metrics Sampler Watchdog`, which runs `harness-metrics.ps1` from a %TEMP% snapshot - not harness-verify.ps1 and not any constants check. (3) Grep for `measured-constants` / `constants.json` across all .mjs, .js and .ps1 in the repo: zero consumers. (4) Grep for the refuted literal `0.81` across all .ps1: two hits, both a COMMENT in harness-verify.ps1 line 201 explaining why the string was removed from the guidance text. So: no consumer, no keeper, no clock, no red path. This file is data with no enforcement behind it yet, and that is stated rather than implied.
